subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which three controls make up the 'exposure triangle' in photography?
questions.explain: The exposure triangle is formed by aperture, shutter speed and ISO, which together control how a photograph is exposed.

questions.q: What is the likely effect of using a wide aperture such as f/2.8?
options: A shallow depth of field with a blurred background
Everything from foreground to background in sharp focus
Increased digital noise across the image
questions.explain: A wide aperture (small f-number) produces a shallow depth of field, keeping the subject sharp while blurring the background.

questions.q: What does the 'rule of thirds' involve?
options: Dividing the frame into a 3x3 grid and placing key elements along the lines or intersections
Using only three colours in a photograph
Taking exactly three shots of every subject
Setting the aperture, shutter and ISO to equal values
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the frame into a 3x3 grid and positions important elements on the lines or their intersections for balanced composition.

questions.q: What is the main effect of using a fast shutter speed?
options: It blurs movement to suggest motion
It increases the depth of field
questions.explain: A fast shutter speed exposes the sensor for a very short time, freezing motion so moving subjects appear sharp.

questions.q: You want to capture a sprinter in crisp focus with no blur during a race. Which setting is most important?
questions.explain: A fast shutter speed freezes the rapid motion of the runner, avoiding motion blur.

questions.q: What does increasing the ISO setting do?
options: Increases the camera's sensitivity to light, but can add noise/grain
Sharpens the focus of the lens
questions.explain: A higher ISO makes the sensor more sensitive to light, useful in low light, but often introduces visible noise or grain.

questions.q: Why might a photographer use 'leading lines' in a composition?
options: To guide the viewer's eye towards the main subject or focal point
To make the image darker overall
questions.explain: Leading lines are compositional lines that draw the viewer's gaze through the image towards the focal point.

questions.q: What is a photogram?
options: An image made by placing objects onto photosensitive paper and exposing it to light, without a camera
A photograph taken on a smartphone
A printed contact sheet of negatives
questions.explain: A photogram is a cameraless image created by placing objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing it to light.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using layers when editing an image digitally?
options: Different elements can be edited separately without permanently altering the others
It converts the image to black and white
It reduces the file size to zero
questions.explain: Layers allow separate elements and adjustments to be worked on independently, giving flexible, non-destructive editing.

questions.q: Which file format stores the most unprocessed image data straight from the camera sensor?
questions.explain: RAW files retain unprocessed sensor data, giving the greatest flexibility for editing exposure and colour.

questions.q: A distracting litter bin appears in the corner of an otherwise strong photograph. Which editing tool would best remove it?
questions.explain: The clone or healing tool samples nearby pixels to paint over and remove unwanted objects seamlessly.

questions.q: What is a photomontage?
options: A single image made by combining parts of several photographs
A photograph printed at very large scale
A camera setting for night photography
questions.explain: A photomontage combines elements from multiple photographs into one composite image.

questions.q: What does 'cropping' an image do?
options: Removes unwanted areas by trimming the edges of the frame
Increases the ISO of the shot
Adds a coloured filter over the whole image
questions.explain: Cropping trims away parts of the image edges to improve composition or remove unwanted content.

questions.q: Ansel Adams is best known for which type of photography?
options: Black-and-white landscapes of the American wilderness
questions.explain: Ansel Adams is famous for his dramatic black-and-white landscape photographs of the American West, such as Yosemite.

questions.q: The idea of the 'decisive moment' is most associated with which photographer and genre?
questions.explain: Henri Cartier-Bresson coined the 'decisive moment', capturing fleeting, telling instants in candid street photography.

questions.q: Cindy Sherman is best known for creating what kind of photographs?
options: Staged self-portraits in which she adopts different characters and roles
questions.explain: Cindy Sherman photographs herself in staged, costumed roles, exploring identity and representation, as in her Untitled Film Stills.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of documentary photography such as Dorothea Lange's 'Migrant Mother'?
options: To record real people and events, often to raise awareness of social conditions
questions.explain: Documentary photography records real events and people, frequently to highlight social issues, as Lange did during the Great Depression.

questions.q: Man Ray is associated with which experimental, cameraless technique (which he called 'rayographs')?
questions.explain: Man Ray produced surrealist photograms, which he named 'rayographs', by placing objects on light-sensitive paper.

questions.q: You want to photograph unposed everyday life in a busy market to tell a true story of the place. Which genre best fits this aim?
questions.explain: Documentary or street photography captures candid, unposed real-life scenes to tell an authentic story.

questions.q: An indoor photograph has come out too dark. Which digital adjustment would most directly correct this?
questions.explain: Raising the brightness or exposure adjustment lightens an underexposed image to reveal detail.
